correctness.rationale: From presence indicators, the indicator covariance formula yields the two exact-moment expressions. All possible systems with total size <=6 are excluded: h<=2 has only one interior effort; s<=2 uses monotonicity in pairwise union size for every effort; for h=3,s<=3 the singleton/two-site decomposition forces tied or same-order variances. With total size 7, only 3x4 and 4x3 remain. The 3-site squared-incidence and endemic-count identities give an independent analytic sign diagnostic. Full finite canonical-mask enumeration covers exactly 42 unlabeled species-site tables in each dimension and four crossing pair-orbits in total (three and one, respectively); exact rational direct-subset moments agree with independently implemented pairwise joint-absence covariance moments. Standalone verify.py returned VERIFY_OK and checks the listed rational counterexample coordinates. No computational finite bound is generalized to larger unenumerated systems.

originality.rationale: Ugland et al. 2003 already derive the general conditional variance and covariance formula; Colwell et al. 2004 already recognize identical occupancy frequency spectra despite different site arrangements. The sole claimed advance is the sharp total-size-seven crossing boundary, its exact four orbit classification and structural three-site sign criterion, not the basic formulas or mean-curve nonidentification. The closest indexed published findings concern iid species discovery or different ecological graph sampling; comparing conclusions does not yield a previously stated exact seven-vertex finite classification. The possibility of unindexed general treatments is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Generic conditional covariance formula makes the counterexamples easily computable and may yield an equivalent unstated corollary in other treatments.
Other potentially unindexed site-based accumulation or graph-incidence classification papers could have independently tabulated the four minimal pairs.
The result concerns fixed finite incidence inventories, not measurement noise, inference from incomplete observation, or biological stability.

value.rationale: Sample-based richness is a standard ecological inventory statistic, and comparing the variability of site-sampling counts at differing effort is meaningful under a common mean curve. The precise seven-vertex minimality, exact four examples modulo relabeling and the any-number-of-species 3-site variance sign test are natural structural delimiters, not a gratuitous chosen matrix slice. They show that risk rankings at shallow sample depths can flip even when species occupancies and entire expected accumulation curves coincide; no ecological prevalence or downstream causal mechanism is claimed.
